segments.text: We get the Selector widget inside the Provider package.
Along with Selector, Provider also gives us widgets like the Consumer widget.
We have already discussed what the notifyListeners method does.
We also covered the difference between context.read and context.watch.
We discussed StreamProvider and FutureProvider as well.
We also learned the difference between listen set to true and false.
All these topics were covered in detail in three to four Provider videos.
So obviously, you should already know the basics.
The Selector widget is the last widget that we are going to cover.
Now the question is, what exactly is the Selector widget?
The main purpose of the Selector widget is to prevent unnecessary rebuilds.
A provider can contain multiple values inside it.
Selector listens to only one specific value from the provider.
Because of this, only the required widget rebuilds.
Now let's move to the practical example and understand this clearly.
On the home screen, we have two widgets: NameScreen and AgeScreen.
We also have two buttons, one to change the name and one to change the age.
Earlier, without Selector, both widgets were rebuilding every time.
Even when we clicked the Change Name button, the Age widget rebuilt.
And when we clicked the Change Age button, the Name widget also rebuilt.
This is called unnecessary rebuilds, and it affects performance.
To confirm this, we added debugPrint statements in both widgets.
Whenever a widget rebuilds, a message appears in the console.
Now let's see how the Selector widget solves this problem.
First, look at the NameScreen widget.
Here, Selector is listening only to the name value from UserProvider.
This means NameScreen will rebuild only when the name changes.
It will completely ignore any changes related to age.
Now look at the AgeScreen widget.
Here, Selector is listening only to the age value.
So AgeScreen will rebuild only when the age changes.
Now let's test this behavior.
When we click the Change Name button, only NameScreen rebuilds.
In the console, you will see only “NameScreen rebuilt”.
The AgeScreen does not rebuild at all.
Now when we click the Change Age button, only AgeScreen rebuilds.
This time, only “AgeScreen rebuilt” is printed.
The NameScreen remains unchanged.
This is how Selector helps us optimize our UI.
Only the required widget rebuilds instead of the whole screen.
This is very important when working on large and complex UIs.
Selector improves performance by avoiding unnecessary rebuilds.
Whenever your provider has multiple values, Selector is very useful.
You should use it when a widget depends on only one value.
This was the complete practical explanation of the Selector widget.
Thank you for watching, and keep practicing Flutter.
